decisions.title: Gym flooring
decisions.chosen: Full rubber matting across the rear gym zone; painted/sealed concrete in the front area
decisions.notes: Options were full rubber vs painted concrete + selective mats. Full rubber wins: continuous tidy look, noise/drop protection for lifting, no mat creep.

decisions.title: Garage door replacement
decisions.notes: Opening is 2587 × 2152 mm. Solid over glazed: secure, insulated, cheaper.

decisions.title: Wall covering
decisions.notes: 14 sheets ordered ($659). Consider clear-seal or whitewash finish rather than paint.

decisions.title: Lighting
decisions.chosen: LED strips in a gap at the top of the plywood + 2 dimmable LED battens

decisions.title: Pull-up setup
decisions.notes: Gymnastic rings on the steel beam are planned. Still deciding whether to also add a ceiling-mounted pull-up bar (2.4 m ceiling — check head clearance).

decisions.title: Which power rack
decisions.notes: Second-hand. Options to weigh: full cage vs half rack vs folding wall-mount (folding saves floor in a 3.9 m-wide room).

decisions.title: Enclosed cupboard vs open racks only
decisions.notes: Enclosed cupboard hides clutter (better for the 'inviting' goal); open racks for grab-every-session items.

notes.title: Space dimensions
notes.body:
Whole garage: 6.2 m long × 3.9 m wide, ceiling 2.4 m.
Rear gym zone: 4.2 × 3.9 m (the 4.2 m walls are the side/long walls).
Front area: 1.5 m long, from the garage door.
Divide between front and rear: 430 × 430 mm pillars on either side, joined by a 300 × 300 mm overhead lintel.
Garage door opening: 2587 mm wide × 2152 mm high.
Steel beam runs down the middle of the ceiling, parallel to the long walls.
Window on the left long wall: 2.1 m from the rear corner, 550 mm wide × ~700 mm high.

notes.title: Finishes
notes.body:
Concrete ceiling painted white.
Walls rendered and painted limestone; being lined with 9mm plywood.
LED strips sit in a gap at the top of the ply.
Floor: bare concrete → rubber matting (rear) + painted/sealed concrete (front).

notes.title: Layout ideas (to pressure-test)
notes.body:
Power rack against a side wall, clear of the beam's drop zone.
Rings on the steel beam = room centreline, keep that floor clear.
Treadmill along the other long wall (2.4 m ceiling OK unless very tall).
Volt trainer + bikes toward the front area.
Mirror panel on the long wall opposite the window to bounce light.
French cleat rail on one ply wall for movable hooks/holders.
